correctness.rationale: For positive solutions conservation gives global existence and x>0. Differentiating Phi=log x-(1+p)y/q-[(1+p)/q+1/s]z cancels y,z and gives Phi_dot=C-r-Dx; independent checks of this exact identity and of dy+dz=rx-qy, dz=rx-sz were replayed from the embedded verify_mean.py (CHECK_OK). If C>r, Phi below L=log((C-r)/(2D))-beta*C has positive derivative >=(C-r)/2, so Phi is bounded below and x eventually uniformly positive; bounded state variables then imply all four per-trajectory Cesaro limits with O(1/T) errors. For periodic or compactly interior invariant measures the exact endpoint coboundaries give strict mean equality. At C=r, xdot<=-x^2 yields x,y,z->0; lambda=-xdot/x->0 makes exponential-filter convolution ratios z/x->r/s and y/x->r/q, valid even q=s; (1/x)dot->D proves sharp t*x->1/D and Phi~ -log t-log D yields the precise logarithmic integral constant. At C<r, xdot/x<=C-r and the linear filters decay, proving log(x)/t->C-r. No finite experiment substitutes for a proof.

value.rationale: This four-species mass-conserving reaction system has a rigorously published parameter regime with a stable equilibrium and nested stable/unstable cycles; equal full-vector time means for these distinct recurrent regimes are mathematically nontrivial and bear on how concentration records distinguish attractors. The exact O(1/T) endpoint controls and universal critical inverse-time coefficients quantify observable macroscopic regimes across the natural mass threshold C=r. The result is not a calculation of the already-known unique equilibrium alone, and does not rely on arbitrary low-importance parameter slices.
